text:
Alex W: Heads-up — after the kernel switch on canary (commit abc123) we saw p95 jumps on streaming chat on a subset of instances. Not across all models, looks correlated with MB size and KV-hit patterns.
Priya N: repro logs?
Alex W: quick summary: p95 went from ~1.2s -> ~2.1s on chat streaming, p99 spikes to ~7-8s in tail. Non-stream completions MB=4 mostly stable.
Jamal R: do you have per-kernel breakdown? fastattn-v2 vs fallback?
Alex W: attaching a quick paste from perf-batcher:
```
model: chat-xl   kernel: fastattn-v2
mb_size=2: p50=230ms p95=1.1s p99=3.2s thrpt=120r/s
mb_size=4: p50=260ms p95=1.3s p99=3.5s thrpt=210r/s
mb_size=1: p50=180ms p95=2.0s p99=7.8s thrpt=60r/s
KV-hit ratio low (<40%) correlates with mb=1 bad tails
```
Sofia L: interesting — streaming handshake + small mb_size exposes KV miss latencies more, because we do immediate kernel invocations per token. KV miss causes extra kernel path + memcpy.
Morgan K: @Alex W can you paste trace id for a p99 event? perf-bot: trace 2026-03-17T15:02:11Z id=trc-0a9f logged.
Alex W: trace id trc-0a9f attached. The critical path shows: handshake -> kernel-select -> KV lookup (miss) -> fallback kernel load -> exec. Fallback kernel load is the heavy part (~4.2s).
Priya N: hypothesis: the kernel selector is choosing fastattn-v2 for mb>1 but streaming with mb=1 triggers fallback-gemv because of sequence-length alignment. Or we hit quantized path mismatch.
Jamal R: we should try two things: (1) force kernel-sampling on canary to prefer stable gemm path for streaming small-mb, (2) enable a short MB hysteresis to avoid immediately dropping to mb=1 on client burst.
Sofia L: also add KV-prefetch for known conversation prefixes — prefetch reduces miss rate. In earlier runs we saw ~60%->85% hit ratio and tail improved dramatically.
Alex W: agreed. Proposed experiment matrix:
- mb sizes: [1,2,4,8]
- kernel hints: [fastattn-v2, gemm-stable]
- kvprefetch: [off,on]
Run steady-state sim for 30m each, 95th/99th and tail count.
Jamal R: include per-request path flagging so we can correlate KV-hit vs kernel change. Add metric tag: kv_hit=true/false, kernel_hint=XYZ, mb_at_dispatch=N.
Morgan K: I'll queue up the canary jobs. One gotcha: we saw SLO regressions only on chat streaming (low tokens per request, many small walks). Non-stream completions (single large response) benefited from batching.
Priya N: for alerting we should change SLO alert to look at p95_streaming_by_model instead of global p95, otherwise we're noise-limited by bulk completions.
Alex W: action items:
- @Jamal R run kernel-hint canary with mb-hysteresis=300ms + kvprefetch on (overnight)
- @Morgan K add metric tags and collect kernel switch latencies
- @Priya N tweak alert rules to separate streaming vs non-streaming p95
- @Sofia L follow up on prefetch heuristics (per-client affinity TTLs)
Jamal R: I'll start the canary now, naming the run mb-hyst-300-khint-gemm. Will post results in the morning.
perf-bot: canary started at 4132110001 id=canary-mb-hyst-300-khint-gemm
Alex W: thanks. If this proves the hypothesis we should implement adaptive MB policy: prefer mb>1 for streaming when KV-hit ratio < threshold OR fall back to stable kernel if fallback loading cost > X ms.
Sofia L: suggestion: keep per-worker KV-affinity TTL of 2s to increase local hit ratio for chat sessions. That should reduce the number of fallback kernel pulls.
Priya N: and add a memory cap on prefetch so we don't blow GPU mem under burst.
Alex W: good point. We'll scope memory budget, per-model.
Morgan K: will capture full traces + kernel load timings. Posting link to run dashboard once done. :eyes:
Alex W: great thread — let's regroup after the canary. :thumbsup:
